claim: The mu(I)-rheology was proposed to model granular flows in the dense inertial regime, with a friction coefficient that varies with the inertial number.
quote: recently proposed to model granular flows in the dense inertial regime

claim: The inertial number I is defined as the ratio of a microscopic grain rearrangement time scale to a macroscopic flow time scale.
quote: ratio of a microscopic grain rearrangement time scale

claim: The paper introduces a bulk friction coefficient mu_b, associated with volume changes, in addition to the usual Coulomb shear friction coefficient mu.
quote: we introduce a bulk friction coefficient µb, associated with volume changes

claim: In the compressible formulation, the strain rate tensor is split into deviatoric and isotropic parts to distinguish isochoric deformations from deformations with net volume change.
quote: splitting the strain rate tensor into deviatoric and isotropic parts

claim: The bulk friction coefficient mu_b directly controls the amplitude of pressure variations in the compressible flow.
quote: directly controls the amplitude of the pressure variations

claim: Little is known about mu_b and its variations with volume fraction, so it is taken as a constant as a first approximation.
quote: as a first approximation, we take it as a constant

claim: The equilibrium relation between pressure and volume fraction plays the role of an equation of state for the granular flow, linking pressure and volume fraction to the kinetic properties of the medium.
quote: plays the role of an equation of state for the granular flow

claim: The paper extends the stability analysis of Barker et al. (2015), which concerned incompressible flows, to compressible flows.
quote: we extend the stability analysis of Barker et al. (2015) to compressible flows

claim: Barker et al. (2015) showed that the mu(I)-rheology is ill-posed in the mathematical sense for a large range of parameters, notably in the low and large inertial number limits.
quote: ill-posed in the mathematical sense for a large range of parameters

claim: In the limit of incompressible flows, the analysis recovers the ill-posed criteria given by Barker et al. (2015).
quote: we recover the ill-posed criteria given by (Barker et al. 2015)

claim: The mu(I)-rheology can be thought of as a generalization of the basic Coulomb friction model, with a friction coefficient that varies according to local shear rate and confinement pressure.
quote: a generalization of the basic Coulomb friction model

claim: At very high inertial numbers, granular flows enter the collisional regime and are best described by kinetic theory.
quote: enter the collisional regime and are best described by kinetic theory

claim: The compressible rheology Eq. (3.9) simplifies to the Jop et al. (2006) incompressible formulation in the case of isochoric deformations.
quote: simplifies to Jop et al. (2006) incompressible formulation

claim: In the limit of small volume changes, the compressible rheology is equivalent to alternative compressible models based on critical state theory (Jackson 1983, Prakash & Rao 1988) or the dilatancy model of Roux & Radjai (1998).
quote: equivalent to alternative compressible models

claim: A similar study by Barker et al. (2017) was published independently, introducing compressibility via the critical state concept borrowed from soil mechanics, while this paper uses a fluid-mechanics formulation based on a second viscosity; both formulations are equivalent and point to the same conclusion.
quote: based on the critical state concept borrowed from soil mechanics

claim: The problem is well-posed if mu_b > 1 - 7*mu/6; below this lower bound the rheology becomes ill-posed.
quote: the problem is well-posed if $\mu _ { b } > 1 - 7 \mu / 6$

claim: Differential problems are termed well-posed if they yield unique solutions depending continuously on the boundary or initial conditions, a distinction attributed to Hadamard.
quote: unique solutions depending continuously on the boundary

claim: When b < 0, one of the roots becomes positive with a growth rate scaling as |xi|^2, indicating ill-posed behaviour of the equations.
quote: one of the roots become positive with a growth rate scaling as

claim: The ill-posed direction is found where b takes a minimum, that is for theta/2 = pi/4.
quote: The ill-posed direction is found where b takes a minimum

claim: The ill-posedness of the system clearly appears for xi_1 > 10, where the growth rate of perturbations dramatically increases as xi_1^2.
quote: The ill-posedness of the system clearly appears for $\xi _ { 1 } > 1 0$

claim: Numerical exploration of the (mu, mu_b) domain found that the condition mu_b >= 1 - 7*mu/6 for well-posedness is verified almost everywhere.
quote: for well-posedeness is verified almost everywhere

claim: Compressibility regularizes mostly the equations, making the problem well-posed for all parameters, with the condition that sufficient dissipation be associated with volume changes.
quote: making the problem well-posed for all parameters

claim: The ill-posed domain defined by Barker et al. (2015) transforms into a domain where the flow is unstable but remains well-posed when compressibility is taken into account.
quote: transforms into a domain where the flow is unstable but remains well-posed

claim: If lambda_3 becomes positive, the flow becomes unstable in the high-wavenumber limit but the problem remains well-posed.
quote: the flow becomes unstable in the high-wavenumber limit

claim: The stability domain in the high-wavenumber limit of compressible flows is independent of flow compressibility phi' and equivalent to the well-posed domain defined by Barker et al. (2015) in the incompressible limit.
quote: is independent of flow compressibility

claim: Compressible shear flows described by a simple constant Coulomb friction (mu' = 0) are always unstable but remain well-posed, since the condition mu_b > 1 - 7*mu/6 is not affected by mu'.
quote: compressible shear flows described by a simple Coulomb friction

claim: The compressible mu(I)-rheology was shown to be unstable for some flow conditions, both at large and small inertial number.
quote: unstable for some flow conditions, both at large and small inertial number

claim: When approaching the random close packing fraction phi_max, the wave speed diverges leading to a flow with infinitely small Mach numbers; close to jamming, decoupling between flow and compressibility waves is likely to occur.
quote: the wave speed diverges leading to a flow with infinitely small Mach numbers

claim: The dynamic compressibility mechanism differs from acoustical wave propagation in static media: in the absence of shear rate, no propagation is possible (c = 0).
quote: in the absence of shear rate, no propagation is possible

claim: The results suggest the importance of taking into account dynamic compressibility for modelling dense granular flows and open new perspectives to investigate acoustic wave emission and propagation inside these flows.
quote: the importance of taking into account dynamic compressibility

claim: The base flow considered is a two-dimensional plane shear in the absence of gravity, with velocity along x_1 and linear in x_2.
quote: We consider for the base flow a two-dimensional plane shear

claim: The base flow solution is perturbed by short-wave normal modes; the normal-mode decomposition is valid in the high-wavenumber limit because perturbation and base flow appear decoupled.

claim: The authors chose to retain the usual incompressible definition of the inertial number, taking the grain density rather than the material density.
quote: chose to retain the usual incompressible definition of the inertial number

claim: The numerical stability problem is discretized in x_2 and solved via a Chebychev collocation method, with the eigenvalue problem solved by the QR algorithm.
quote: solved numerically via a Chebychev collocation method

claim: No-slip and no-penetration boundary conditions are imposed at x_2 = +/-1/2 for the perturbed velocity in the numerical solution.
quote: No-slip and no-penetration boundary conditions are imposed
